Below is a practical, reusable Python scraper you can use to crawl a docs site (like https://docs.freepik.com/introduction), extract the page content, and write a directory tree of .md files based on the URL path. The script:

- Respects robots.txt
- Limits request rate (configurable)
- Follows internal links only (same host & under the docs base path)
- Attempts to convert the HTML body to Markdown (via markdownify) and falls back to plain text if unavailable
- Builds folders according to URL path segments and writes a sanitized filename

Adjust the CSS selectors and other small settings to match a specific docs site's HTML structure.

Script (save as crawl_docs.py):


```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
crawl_docs.py

Crawl docs starting at BASE_URL and save pages to an output directory,
mapping URL path segments to subfolders and saving content as Markdown files.

Usage: python crawl_docs.py
"""

import os
import time
import re
import sys
from collections import deque
from urllib.parse import urlparse, urljoin, urldefrag

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from urllib import robotparser

# Optional: for nicer Markdown conversion. If not installed the script will fall back to plain text.
try:
    from markdownify import markdownify as html2md
except Exception:
    html2md = None

# -------------------- CONFIG --------------------
BASE_URL = "https://docs.freepik.com/introduction"   # starting page
OUTPUT_DIR = "FreepikAPI"                            # root directory to create
USER_AGENT = "DocsScraper/1.0 (+https://example.com)" # set to your contact info ideally
REQUEST_DELAY = 0.5  # seconds between requests
MAX_PAGES = None      # optional: stop after this many pages (None => unlimited)

# CSS selectors to extract the main content and the page title.
# These may need to be adjusted to match the target docs site's HTML.
TITLE_SELECTOR = "h1"
CONTENT_SELECTOR_CANDIDATES = [
    "main",                      # typical modern doc layout
    "article",                   # some docs
    "div.markdown",              # Docusaurus-like classes
    "div.theme-doc-markdown",    # another pattern
    "div.docs-content",
    "div[class*='content']"
]
# Only follow links under this prefix; default to base URL's origin + path root
# e.g. for https://docs.freepik.com/introduction we probably want to keep under:
DOCS_PREFIX = "{scheme}://{netloc}".format(
    scheme=urlparse(BASE_URL).scheme, netloc=urlparse(BASE_URL).netloc
)

# -------------------------------------------------

session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update({"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})


def sanitize_name(name: str, max_len: int = 200) -> str:
    # Make a safe filesystem name
    name = name.strip()
    # replace invalid chars
    name = re.sub(r'[<>:"/\\|?*\x00-\x1F]+', "-", name)
    # collapse whitespace
    name = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", name)
    # cut length
    return name[:max_len].strip(" -._")


def ensure_dir(path: str):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)


def choose_content_selector(soup):
    for sel in CONTENT_SELECTOR_CANDIDATES:
        node = soup.select_one(sel)
        if node:
            return node
    # fallback to body
    return soup.body


def is_same_site(url: str, base_netloc: str):
    try:
        p = urlparse(url)
        return (p.netloc == base_netloc) or (p.netloc == "")
    except Exception:
        return False


def check_robots(base_url: str, user_agent: str) -> robotparser.RobotFileParser:
    parsed = urlparse(base_url)
    robots_url = f"{parsed.scheme}://{parsed.netloc}/robots.txt"
    rp = robotparser.RobotFileParser()
    rp.set_url(robots_url)
    try:
        rp.read()
    except Exception:
        # If robots can't be read, be conservative but continue
        print(f"Warning: couldn't read robots.txt at {robots_url}; continuing.")
    return rp


def to_markdown(html: str) -> str:
    if html2md:
        return html2md(html, heading_style="ATX")
    # fallback: very simple cleanup
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")
    return soup.get_text("\n", strip=True)


def url_to_path_and_filename(base_url: str, page_url: str):
    # Map path segments to folders. Example:
    # https://docs.freepik.com/introduction -> OUTPUT_DIR/introduction/Overview.md
    # https://docs.freepik.com/apis/image-gen/mystic/create -> OUTPUT_DIR/apis/image-gen/mystic/Create.md
    parsed_base = urlparse(base_url)
    parsed = urlparse(page_url)
    # use only path on target
    path = parsed.path or "/"
    parts = [p for p in path.strip("/").split("/") if p]
    # If page is the root (no parts) use "Overview"
    if len(parts) == 0:
        folder_parts = []
        filename = "Overview"
    else:
        # treat last segment as filename, the rest as folders
        folder_parts = parts[:-1]
        filename = parts[-1]
        # often docs use "index" or similar -> make nicer
        if filename.lower() in ("index", "readme"):
            filename = "Overview"

    # include query parameters lightly in filename when they exist (rare for docs)
    if parsed.query:
        filename = f"{filename}-{re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9-_.]', '-', parsed.query)[:50]}"

    # decode some percent-encoding and sanitize
    filename = sanitize_name(filename)
    # Capitalize first letter of filename and use .md
    filename = filename[:1].upper() + filename[1:] if filename else "Page"
    rel_dir = os.path.join(*[sanitize_name(p) for p in folder_parts]) if folder_parts else ""
    return rel_dir, filename + ".md"


def save_page(output_root: str, rel_dir: str, filename: str, title: str, content_md: str, source_url: str):
    target_dir = os.path.join(output_root, rel_dir) if rel_dir else output_root
    ensure_dir(target_dir)
    path = os.path.join(target_dir, filename)
    header = f"# {title}\n\n_Source: {source_url}_\n\n"
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(header)
        f.write(content_md)
    print("Saved:", path)


def crawl(start_url: str, output_root: str, docs_prefix: str, max_pages=None):
    parsed_start = urlparse(start_url)
    base_netloc = parsed_start.netloc

    rp = check_robots(start_url, USER_AGENT)

    q = deque([start_url])
    visited = set()
    pages_count = 0

    while q:
        url = q.popleft()
        if url in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(url)

        # respect robots
        try:
            if rp and not rp.can_fetch(USER_AGENT, url):
                print("Skipping (robots.txt):", url)
                continue
        except Exception:
            # if robot parser failed, just continue
            pass

        print("Fetching:", url)
        try:
            resp = session.get(url, timeout=20)
        except Exception as e:
            print("Failed to fetch", url, ":", e)
            continue

        if resp.status_code != 200:
            print("Non-200:", resp.status_code, url)
            continue

        soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "html.parser")

        # Extract title
        title_tag = soup.select_one(TITLE_SELECTOR)
        title = title_tag.get_text(strip=True) if title_tag else (soup.title.string if soup.title else url)

        content_node = choose_content_selector(soup)
        # If there is no meaningful content node, fallback to reading the whole body
        if content_node:
            content_html = str(content_node)
        else:
            content_html = resp.text

        content_md = to_markdown(content_html)

        # Map to output path
        rel_dir, filename = url_to_path_and_filename(start_url, url)
        save_page(output_root, rel_dir, filename, title, content_md, url)

        pages_count += 1
        if max_pages and pages_count >= max_pages:
            print("Reached max pages limit. Stopping.")
            break

        # find internal links to follow
        for a in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
            href = a.get("href")
            # skip javascript: anchors
            if href.startswith("javascript:") or href.startswith("mailto:") or href.startswith("tel:"):
                continue
            joined = urljoin(url, href)
            # remove fragment
            joined, _ = urldefrag(joined)
            # only follow same site and under docs prefix
            parsed_joined = urlparse(joined)
            if not is_same_site(joined, base_netloc):
                continue
            # optionally restrict to docs prefix + path (prevents jumping to main site)
            if not joined.startswith(docs_prefix):
                continue
            if joined not in visited:
                q.append(joined)

        time.sleep(REQUEST_DELAY)

    print("Crawl finished. Pages saved:", pages_count)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # create output root dir
    ensure_dir(OUTPUT_DIR)
    crawl(BASE_URL, OUTPUT_DIR, DOCS_PREFIX, max_pages=MAX_PAGES)
```

How it structures files:
- For a URL like /apis/imagegeneration/mystic/create the script will create FreepikAPI/apis/imagegeneration/mystic/Create.md
- For the base root /introduction it will create FreepikAPI/introduction/Overview.md (you can tweak naming logic if you prefer a different layout)
- Each file starts with an H1 title (from the page's h1 or title) and a Source link, followed by the page content converted to markdown (if markdownify is available) or plain text.

Dependencies
- requests
- beautifulsoup4
- optional: markdownify (pip install markdownify) for nicer Markdown conversion

Install:
pip install requests beautifulsoup4 markdownify

Customization tips
- If the docs are built with Docusaurus or another framework, inspect a page and adapt CONTENT_SELECTOR_CANDIDATES and TITLE_SELECTOR for more accurate extraction (e.g. "div.theme-doc-markdown > article").
- If you want the folder structure to follow the visual sidebar grouping rather than URL path segments, you'll need to parse the site's nav/sidebar structure (often present in a specific container). You can locate the sidebar element and use it to determine parent sections for a page; the approach will be site-specific.
- Increase REQUEST_DELAY to be more polite; consider adding random jitter.
- Respect Terms of Service and robots.txt. Don't overload the site. When in doubt, ask the site owner for a copy.

If you want, I can:
- Modify the script to follow the exact Freepik docs HTML structure (if you copy one page's source or tell me the specific classes for the main content and sidebar),
- Add a CLI argument parser (argparse) to pass base_url and output_dir,
- Make it export HTML instead of Markdown, or include front-matter metadata.
